h1: P24 at Kaset — The Loft Boutique Directly Opposite Kasetsart University with Bangkok's Best Staff Score
intro: If you need a clean, characterful place to stay near Kasetsart University that won't drain your wallet and puts you five minutes from the BTS, P24 at Kaset is the name that keeps appearing in real guest reviews. Sitting on Soi Phahonyothin 36, directly opposite the Bangkhen campus of Kasetsart University, BTS Sena Nikhom station is just ~400 m away — a comfortable five-minute walk. The 26-room property wraps a Thai-industrial-loft aesthetic around competitive pricing: from around ฿800 per night. A score of 8.7/10 from 140 Trip.com reviews — and an almost-perfect 9.8 for staff on Booking.com — signals this small hotel punches well above its weight in this neighbourhood.

body.html: A small hotel that lets its reviews do the talking — P24 at Kaset opened in 2016 on Soi Phahonyothin 36 in the Sena Nikhom sub-district of Chatuchak, directly across from the main gates of Kasetsart University's Bangkhen campus. The name "P24" references Phahonyothin Road, the major artery the soi branches off. With just 26 rooms and a score of 8.7/10 on Trip.com (140 reviews) alongside 8.4 on Agoda (129 reviews), the property achieves a ratio of satisfaction-to-scale that many larger Bangkok hotels never reach. The guests who typically stay here, according to those same reviews: visiting parents of KU students, overseas exchange academics, couples wanting a design-forward base north of the city centre, and budget-savvy travellers who need the BTS within reach.

Location and transport — P24 at Kaset's biggest selling point, repeated across almost every review, is that BTS Sena Nikhom station (Green Line) is only ~400 m away — around five minutes on foot. From Sena Nikhom you can reach Siam in about 20 minutes; Mo Chit (Chatuchak Weekend Market) is just five or six stops. The hotel sits directly opposite Kasetsart University's main entrance, making it essentially on-campus for anyone with university business. Kaset intersection, Ngam Wong Wan Road, and the university's commercial strip are all within short walking or motorbike-taxi distance. Don Mueang International Airport (DMK) is approximately 14 km away — around 20–25 minutes by car or expressway. One practical note: Soi Phahonyothin 36 is a narrow side lane and the hotel signage is not highly visible from the main road — taxi and Grab drivers sometimes miss it on a first visit.

"Room was spotless and much better designed than expected for the price. The cafe downstairs is a lovely touch. BTS is genuinely just a few minutes' walk — stayed here for a week of meetings at Kasetsart and would book again without hesitation."

Design and rooms — P24 at Kaset takes a noticeably different aesthetic direction from the functional 3-star properties that dominate this part of Bangkok. The interior language is Thai-industrial loft: exposed brick walls, steel columns, high ceilings, warm timber accents and locally commissioned artwork. TripAdvisor and Trip.com reviewers consistently single out the look of the rooms as a highlight, often using phrases like "much nicer than I expected" and "actually looks like the photos." The two room categories are Standard Twin (two single beds with window) for friends or colleagues sharing, and Double Bed Room (one double) for couples or solo travellers who prefer more sleeping space. All rooms include air conditioning, mini-fridge, 32-inch LCD TV, private balcony, hot shower, complimentary water and free Wi-Fi. Two caveats from real reviews worth knowing: some rooms have low ceilings, and a handful of beds are shorter than standard — guests over 180 cm should ask about bed length before booking. There is no elevator: upper-floor rooms require stair access.

Facilities and atmosphere — The most-mentioned amenity beyond location is the on-site cafe on the ground floor, which reviewers describe as a pleasant place to start the day or catch up on laptop work between BTS trips. Free parking is available on-site for guests — not a large lot, but meaningful in Bangkok and appreciated in reviews. The property's resident cats appear in multiple reviews with an affectionate note, a tiny signal of the informal, welcoming energy that distinguishes a genuinely boutique hotel from one that merely calls itself one. A deposit of ฿1,000 is collected at check-in and returned on departure. Wi-Fi is free throughout but received a notably lower score — 6.7/10 on Booking.com — than any other category, suggesting it can be inconsistent under load. Heavy remote workers should bring a mobile hotspot as backup.

What real guests say — Synthesised from Trip.com (140 reviews, 8.7/10; cleanliness 8.9, location 8.7, service 8.7) and Booking.com (56 reviews; staff 9.8, location 9.3, value 9.0, cleanliness 8.7, facilities 8.4, Wi-Fi 6.7). Consistent praise: staff warmth and helpfulness — the 9.8 staff score on Booking is unusually high for any price tier; room design that feels genuinely well-considered; cleanliness; the walkability to BTS and to university facilities; the cafe. Consistent caveats: the narrow soi entrance and low-profile signage making navigation difficult on arrival; the absence of an elevator; occasional Wi-Fi drops; some rooms missing an electric kettle and safe. One March 2025 Booking review flagged a cleanliness concern and odours — out of character with the general pattern but worth noting for completeness.

Pricing and value — Standard Twin and Double rooms start from approximately ฿800–900 per night in regular periods, rising to ฿1,000–1,200 during university events (graduation ceremonies, the annual Ag Fair) or long public-holiday weekends. At this price point, for a designed room with a working AC, private balcony, free parking and a BTS station five minutes away, P24 at Kaset represents solid value for Bangkok's northern arc. The honest qualification: Kaset-Nawamin is not a tourist neighbourhood. If your days are centred on Siam, Sukhumvit or Chinatown, commuting from here takes 20–30 minutes each way. But if Kasetsart University, Paolo Hospital, or the Green Line corridor north of Mo Chit is where your business lies, this hotel hits the brief neatly and affordably.

honestSummary: P24 at Kaset is a small, thoughtfully designed hotel that delivers where it counts — clean rooms with genuine character, an almost-perfect staff score, walkable BTS access and honest pricing. The honest caveats are real: no elevator, occasional Wi-Fi drops, and a side-street entrance that catches first-time visitors off guard. If those are dealbreakers, look elsewhere; if they aren't, this property is a strong choice for anyone with business in the Kaset corridor.
honestChecks: If you have heavy luggage or reduced mobility — there is no elevator at P24 at Kaset. Upper-floor rooms are stair-access only. Request a ground-floor room at check-in; it's usually possible when availability allows.

If reliable Wi-Fi for video calls or heavy remote work is non-negotiable — the Wi-Fi here scores only 6.7/10 on Booking.com, significantly below the hotel's scores in every other category. Bring a 4G/5G mobile hotspot as a backup.

If you're arriving by taxi or Grab for the first time — Soi Phahonyothin 36 is narrow and the hotel sign is not easily visible from Phahonyothin Road. Tell your driver 'opposite the main gate of Kasetsart University Bangkhen' — that landmark lands every time.

tips.title: Navigate by the University Gate, Not the Soi Number
tips.body: When directing a taxi or Grab, say 'opposite the main gate of Kasetsart University Bangkhen.' The soi number alone often confuses drivers unfamiliar with the area.

tips.title: BTS Sena Nikhom — Turn Left Out of the Hotel
tips.body: Turn left from the hotel entrance, walk to Phahonyothin Road, then continue to BTS Sena Nikhom station — around 400 m, five minutes at a relaxed pace. No motorbike taxi needed.

tips.title: Request a Lower-Floor Room if You Have Heavy Bags
tips.body: There is no lift. If you're arriving with large suitcases or have any mobility concerns, ask at check-in for a ground-floor room — staff are noted for being accommodating.

tips.title: The Ground-Floor Cafe Opens Early
tips.body: The in-hotel cafe on the ground floor opens early — ideal for a coffee before heading to the BTS. Pricing is reasonable and the atmosphere beats most chain-hotel breakfast rooms at this price point.

faqTitle: P24 at Kaset Bangkok — Frequently Asked Questions

faq.q: Where is P24 at Kaset and how close is the BTS?
faq.a: P24 at Kaset is on Soi Phahonyothin 36, Sena Nikhom, Chatuchak, Bangkok — directly opposite the main gate of Kasetsart University Bangkhen. BTS Sena Nikhom station (Green Line) is approximately 400 m away, a 5-minute walk. From Sena Nikhom, Siam takes around 20 minutes and Mo Chit about 5–6 stops.

faq.q: What is the price range at P24 at Kaset?
faq.a: Rates start from approximately ฿800–900 per night for Standard Twin or Double rooms in regular periods. Prices can rise to ฿1,000–1,200 during university events (graduation, Ag Fair) or long public-holiday weekends. Compare across Agoda, Booking.com and Trip.com before reserving.

faq.q: Does P24 at Kaset have free parking?
faq.a: Yes, free on-site parking is available for guests. The lot is not large, so if you're arriving during a major Kasetsart University event, it's worth contacting the hotel in advance to confirm a space.

faq.q: Is there an elevator at P24 at Kaset?
faq.a: No — P24 at Kaset does not have a lift. Upper-floor rooms require stair access. If you have heavy luggage or any mobility limitation, request a ground-floor room at check-in; staff are noted for being helpful about this.

faq.q: Who is P24 at Kaset best suited for?
faq.a: It's an excellent fit for visiting parents of Kasetsart University students, overseas academics on exchange, couples who want a well-designed budget base on the Green Line, and anyone with business in the Kaset-Nawamin corridor. It is less well-suited to travellers planning multiple daily excursions into central Bangkok, for whom a more central location saves meaningful commuting time.
